utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa, are you ready for the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gavric.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to start off briefly by asking you how long you knew Colonel Blagojevic. How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him before he arrived in the Bratunac Brigade, when he was a lower-ranking officer. And I knew him in my private life because we originate from the same place, lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say he was a lower-ranking officer, where was he working before he came to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic was in the Drina Corps. After that, he came to the Bratunac Brigade. As far as I know previously, I think he served in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you say you've known him from your private life. So did you grow up with him?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He's older than me. He is my brother's generation; they're about ten years older than me. As I was younger, I knew the older people, of course, better than I knew the younger ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell us, sir, what was his position in the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think he was an engineers man. I assumed that because we never actually discussed this topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. How did you know then that he was a lower-ranking officer in the corps?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You misunderstood me or perhaps I didn't explain it very well. I knew him previously, before he arrived in the Drina Corps, when he was serving in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Do you consider him a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't consider someone a personal friend unless you socialise every day, but yes I would say he was a friend in any case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, I'd like to go back to the -- what we -- what you briefly discussed yesterday relating to the artillery. And I understand during the period of 6 and 11 July you said that your units were located in the area in the rear behind the front end of the Bratunac Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you misunderstood that. Our units were behind the front end of the Bratunac Brigade, and that's as it should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And from your position, sir, could you actually see Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Extremely well and very precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You could see the buildings there. Right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you understood my testimony yesterday, I was far away from Potocari as a village. As the crow flies, it was about 2 and a half to 3 kilometres away or 2 and a half to 3.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. My question was: You could see the buildings in Potocari. You just told us that you could see Potocari very well. Right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see every important building in Potocari from that observation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you see the impact of artillery falling around Potocari or in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every hit and every projectile fired from our positions was something I could see. That's how it's supposed to be done. You cannot just fire off the top of your head; you have to see where the projectiles fall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, you testified, sir, that you could also see the road where the Muslims were walking towards Potocari. Do you remember telling us that, you saw those Muslims walking towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the rounds that were dropping near the Muslims as they were walking towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single round fell near the Muslims walking along the road toward Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, do you know why then the DutchBat and the Muslims would say that there were rounds being dropped near the Muslims toward Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we're going to conduct this kind of cross-examination, as I've said last week and I keep -- continue to say, especially when Ms. Issa does cross-examination, she can point to the record, who said what, and give him an opportunity. And I think there's -- there must be a disconnect as well because the gentleman is under the impression that his hits are in that direction. But if she's going to go in that direction, she should at least say, "So-and-so said such-and-such, what do you say?" As opposed to paraphrasing what she understands the testimony to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, I think there's some problem in your question. You just asked the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour. I will try to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that members of the DutchBat and Muslim population said in their statements to the -- to investigators and testimony that there were rounds being dropped around the Muslims as they were walking towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour. Who are these DutchBat? What are these Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Same problem, Ms. Issa. Put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I asked him if he was aware of that. I'm not sure of what you're trying to tell me. I didn't think that was speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mean to be disputatious and I certainly don't want to be disruptive to Ms. Issa's cross, but generally speaking, if one is going to pose that question they would have readily available a part of the transcript or a statement that would say such-and-such. So in the event some disputatious lawyer like myself jumps up and objects, they can say, well, it's right here. But in all fairness to this witness, they could just say, the DutchBat who was there said such-and-such, you're telling us today this and that. Now, could you give us an explanation. That way on the record we don't have the lawyer's representation what's in the testimony, but we have the actual record, where it is, who said what, and the witness then can be given a fair opportunity to answer. That's all I'm asking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, you may put a very simple question to this witness just to say that: Do you know the reactions of the Muslim population when they were walking towards Potocari like this?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour. I'll take Your Honour's suggestion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you able to see how the Muslims were reacting as they were walking towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the citizens of Srebrenica who were moving from the direction of Srebrenica towards Bratunac, or rather, the industrial zone where they stopped, walked normally without any panic, at a normal pace, because nobody from our side was disturbing them in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're telling us, sir, that they didn't look like they were afraid as they were going to Potocari? You didn't see any fear or panic or chaos on the part of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see that because you can see fear or panic in someone's face if you see them from close up, not from 2.000 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you just told us that they walked normally towards Potocari. How did you know they were walking normally, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You consider that a man is walking normally when they are walking, not running, when they're not walking too slow or too fast. If a man goes 4 or 5 kilometres an hour, that means he's walking normally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's your definition of it. Moving on then to another area, sir. Did any communication occur between you and the command on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What command are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade, sir, your command.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 11th, I went out in the morning to the observation post, and I did not contact anyone from the Bratunac Brigade command from the observation post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had no communication about the NATO planes, no warnings that the NATO planes were in the area?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally saw the NATO planes from my observation post at about 1300 hours, when they were flying over the firing area of my unit, the town of Bratunac, and the town of Srebrenica. At one point, I noticed a plane falling, or rather, firing two rockets. I just noticed a lot of thick smoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But before you saw that, sir, you didn't receive any communication from the command that NATO planes were -- or had just arrived or were arriving or were coming. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive this. I was at the front end, near the front end, where I would have been among the first to observe the arrival of NATO planes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. And did you not contact the command and let them know that you observed the arrival of the NATO planes?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't contact the command. I didn't report to them, because there was another unit whose duty it was to observe the air space and to report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I thought you just said, sir, you were one of the first people to observe the NATO planes. Didn't you think it was your obligation to contact the command and let them know?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Turning then to the 6th of July report, sir, the daily combat report that you looked at yesterday. And maybe we can look at it again just to refresh our memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may be of some assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This one is in complete working order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That would be very helpful. It seems to be falling apart here, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just record, the report we're looking at is exhibit number P411. Now, we looked at this yesterday, sir, and in particular I think Mr. Karnavas drew your attention to paragraph 2, the second part of that paragraph 2, which states: "Firing support against set targets was provided by 50 kilogrammes shell launcher (school in Potocari, 11 of March factory, and the wide area of the village of Potocari)" And I understand, sir, that you explained - and I'm going to go straight to your statement, testimony - that there was an error made by the duty officer in drafting this report. And I think you stated at page 32, line 19, of your testimony: "To clarify, within the composition of the brigade, there is a brigade artillery; whereas, I said there is a 122-millimetre gun battery; 105-millimetre Howitzer; and B1 76-millimetre guns. Within the battalion, as battalion artillery support, there are platoons of 82-millimetre mortars; 120-millimetre mortars; and recoilless guns. "Looking at this paragraph of the combat report," and you're referring to the 7th of July, "I can see that the duty officer who drew up this report does not distinguish between the battalion firing group and the brigade artillery group." Do you remember saying that, giving us that explanation? Did you hear my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter has not finished interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do remember and if necessary, I can explain it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That won't be necessary, sir, I just wanted to refresh our memories as to what your testimony was yesterday, all right? Now, according to the UNMO report, and I'm going to specifically refer to the July 6th report, the UNMO report basically states, and this is at Exhibit 782 for the record, tab 10: "Team Srebrenica reported a BSA offensive launched and ongoing within the enclave as reported under separate cover. The BSA used tanks, artillery, mortars, rockets, and have targeted the DutchBat headquarters. The Bandera triangle, the DutchBat OPs, U and S, and south of OP H, the Potocari township, the Srebrenica township." Now, in this report, sir, they are referring to more than simply mortars or recoilless guns. They're referring to artillery and tanks and rockets. Right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tanks were not under my command. If they fired from somewhere, I am unaware of it. 120-millimetre mortars, that was the calibre of my guns; the same calibre, detonation, destructive power. So what your report says, I know that from my observation post and my unit, we did not observe this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, sir, it's not my report, it's the UNMO report. And, in addition to tanks, they also referred to artillery and rockets. Now, didn't you testify yesterday that the rocket platoon was under your command?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was under my command but that I did not issue orders for it to fire. And I don't remember that it fired at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the artillery, sir? Was that not part of your unit?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I explained that the 82-millimetre mortars and the 120-millimetre mortars were in the artillery group for support of infantry battalions; they were not part of the brigade artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, well the report, sir, specifically refers to -- makes a distinction between artillery and mortars. That's the point, sir. So mortars refers to the battalion infantry units, and artillery would refer to your unit, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to reiterate. The brigade artillery consisted of a 105-millimetre Howitzer battery, a gun platoon, 122-M 31 through 31 and B176-millimetre battery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, there's another report also in July 1995, and I believe it refers to 6 July. And it specifically states: "The Potocari compound was targeted several times during the day. It was hit by several tank -- tanks which caused great damage to the watchtower. No UN casualties were reported and Srebrenica enclave, and artillery impact killed a civilian and injured a boy." Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The 7 July UNMO report states: "Team Srebrenica reported that the Bosnian Serb army continued their offensive on the enclave with heavy weapons since early this morning. DutchBat reported heavy shelling around their compound in Potocari, and as a result three men were injured and brought by MSF to the hospital." It continues on. And at the end it says: "We cannot analyse the craters at the moment due to the continuous shelling, but we assess that the Bosnian Serb army are still using mortars, rockets, artillery, and tanks." Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. 8 July. The report states: "Shelling started in Srebrenica village this morning at 8.00. They seem to be concentrating more on the densely populated areas like Potocari town and CP 640847." Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 9 July report states: "UNMO team Srebrenica reportedly heard 78 explosions in Srebrenica town alone. More than 70 per cent of the explosions were in the centre of the town." Are you aware of that occurring on 9 July?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 10 July report states: "Two heavy shells, probably 155-millimetre artillery shells, hit the direct surrounding of the hospital at 1100 hours. All the windows are smashed and shrapnel had showered the walls and rooms of the hospital. The surgery is very difficult to proceed. The number of casualties and wounded we don't know yet, but we will inform you as soon as possible. It looks as if the Bosnian Serb army are now targeting the hospital and the surroundings. This means also our former location, PTT building, is now not safe to return to. More to follow." Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, sir, just to give you a little more specificity on that same day, 10 July, the report states that: "The Srebrenica township is still undergoing a very heavy shelling. So far we have recorded figures of 49 shells since 1250 hours to 1353 hours. This afternoon with figure 9 rockets launched into the town and exchanges of occasionally HMG and SA firing. We estimate the current situation to be getting worse." Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And although you said you were able to observe the buildings in Potocari, were you not able to see the impact on those buildings?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about the hits in Srebrenica around the hospital, post office, and densely populated town area. From my observation post, you couldn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that was a different question, though, sir. The question was: You weren't able to see any impact in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not see any impact in Potocari, none at all, until I worked with my artillery on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, I think you testified yesterday that between the 6th and 11 July you did not fire into the enclave. Did you fire into the enclave before the 6th of July, before that period?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 17th of April, 1993, the Army of Republika Srpska, or rather, the Bratunac Brigade did not fire at all in the direction of the enclave until 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Turning then to the exhibit P397, and I'm going to ask Madam Usher to provide you with the copy of the B/C/S. Perhaps we can put the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, for the record, the previous exhibit was P782, tab 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before we go to that, can you just clarify when in 1995. You said that the Bratunac Brigade did not fire at all in the direction of the enclave until 1995. When did they start firing in the direction of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade, I'm talking about the Bratunac artillery battery, in fact, did not fire in the direction of the enclave until the 11th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then go to that exhibit which is P397. And I believe it's -- you have the B/C/S version in front of you and it's now on the ELMO. Now, if we look at paragraph 2, first of all that's dated 25 May, 1995, at the top. Do you see that there? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you look at paragraph 2, the first line of that paragraph says: "Our forces did not open fire towards the demilitarised zone," and it goes on. Now, from reading that, sir, does that mean that on occasion the Bratunac Brigade did open fire on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, all the combat reports which were written on the 17th of March, 1993 - and that's how it was - up until the beginning of the operation in 1995, in the month of July, there is this point that says: "Our forces did not open fire," during that period of time. So that paragraph is contained in all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So what does it mean, sir? Are you saying that it doesn't mean that on occasion the brigade has opened fire?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A moment ago when I was explaining this, I said that from the 17th of March, 2003 [as interpreted], until July 1995, as the enclave was not fired at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's go to the next exhibit, P855. Now, we're just putting the English version on the ELMO. Now, that's dated 25 May, 1995. Strictly confidential. It says: "Very urgent," and addressed to the Drina Corps. Now, do you see your name down there at the bottom of this letter? It says: "Artillery chief, Captain Mico Gavric."

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. It has my signature. May I just be allowed to read through it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. Go ahead. All right. I'm just going to read it so we all -- we're all on the same page. It states: "At 1907 hours, we opened fire on Srebrenica on Colonel Lazic's orders. As the first missile was being fired from the 105-millimetre Howitzer, number 1120, the recoil was greater than usual and the back section became stuck in the back position. It is necessary that you immediately send artillery repairmen to our brigade to fix this fault." Now, it appears, sir, that according to you on May 25th, 1995, you fired on Srebrenica. Isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that on the 25th -- I can guarantee now as to what was fired at in a certain locality. I am trying to rewind the film in my mind. But this document isn't clear to me. It appears that I signed it. I know that there was back recoil and I had some people injured. Now, as far as I can remember - I can't believe that it was in 1995, although, yes, indeed it does say in 1995 - an enemy tank did fire at us from the front of the Muslim defence lines, from the first Muslim defence lines. And probably, 99 per cent certainty, we probably did respond. Now, the anti-armour and anti-armour projectile was used to try to destroy the tank. Well, I suppose I wrote this, but I really don't remember that that was in 1995 at all. I really can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, you wrote it and it's dated 1995, so I think it's safe to say that that's what happened in 1995. Right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the date, yes; but judging by my recollections, no. I remember that people were injured and I remember that this back section became stuck and so on. When I think about it now and turn my mind back to those days, I remember that we were fired at from the Budak defence lines by an enemy tank on my fire positions, because there was a group that had been filtered in, a group of their reconnaissance men. And when we saw this fire, we did target the tank, but I really don't remember that that was in 1995. And if it says we opened fire, then I suppose we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then go to the next exhibit. That's P856/A, for the record. I think that's the English version. I'm just providing you, sir, with the B/C/S copy. Now, that's again from the command of the Bratunac Brigade marked strictly confidential dated 25 May 1995. And it appears to be an interim combat report. Do you see that there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it -- and on the bottom it says: "Commander Vidoje Blagojevic." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we look at the first paragraph, sir, it appears to be an interim combat report to the command of the Drina Corps. And it states: "Pursuant to Colonel Lazic's verbal order, we fired two times, two projectiles (in total four) from Howitzer 105-millimetre on the Srebrenica town. Projectiles were fired at 1907 hours. Artillery observers from Pribicevac reported that two projectiles fell in the vicinity of the Domavija building. Other two projectiles were not observed, but they definitely fell in Srebrenica." Now, that appears to relate to the same incident that you noted in the previous report that we just saw. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This combat report was probably compiled on the basis of this section, this passage, where I said that the equipment had broken down. But I really can't remember -- I remember a lot, but I really can't remember this. I just can't remember the period, whether it was 1995. I just don't remember it being in May 1995. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well perhaps, sir, we can then move on to another area. Did you participate, sir, in the demining of the Zuti Most area on 11 July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember doing that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that if it says so somewhere in some document that I have -- that a man of the same age and the same name and he worked as an engineer's man, but we have -- we're not related at all. But I do know that such a man exists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me refer you to the passage so we can clear that up. We can go to Exhibit P159, page 2. Now, sir, what was the rank of this man that you just mentioned who may have the same name?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think his name is Milos Gavric. Whether he had a rank or not, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this is the report which has a signature on the bottom that says Ljubisa Borovcanin at the very end of the report. And if we look at paragraph 2, at page 2, you see that it says: "Between 0500 and 0630 hours, the pioneers of the Bratunac Brigade, led by Captain Gavric, cleared a passage through a minefield or groups of mines towards Budak or immediately around the Zuti Most/Potocari road. Members of the 1st Company of the Zvornik special police unit, led by a pioneer from the Bratunac Brigade, set off through the cleared passages towards Potocari to concrete conditions for the introduction of hardware. As personnel were being introduced, a sapper stepped on a PROM, anti-personnel bouncing fragmentation mine. He was taken to the Bratunac health centre, where he died." And then it goes on. Do you recall this incident?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer a moment ago was correct. It was Milos Gavric. I don't think he had the rank of captain, just Gavric. And I remember that that particular unit was -- did do the demining of this area and that one of the soldiers was killed. I think it was from the 2nd Battalion, an engineer's man. I know nothing more than that. It was to the left of my observation post; I wasn't able to see all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Milos Gavric, you're saying, is part of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade? Is that what you were just saying? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the soldier who was killed I assume was from the 2nd Battalion, and I think they had an engineer's department in that battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where -- what unit was Milos Gavric part of?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade, yes. Now, whether he was part of the 2nd Battalion or an independent unit, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you have an officer at the brigade command? Or at that time did you have an office at the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at this document, I'm surprised how come it says Milos Gavric when there was a second lieutenant by the name of Pejic, as far as I recall who was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, it doesn't say Milos Gavric; we just want to be clear for the record. It says Captain Gavric. That's what it says. Right? That's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says Captain Gavric in the document, yes. But you probably thought it was me, but it wasn't. And I never worked on this demining process. I'm not an engineer's man. There was an engineer's office in the brigade. So all I know is to the best of my recollections is that Milos Gavric at one point was a part of that engineer's unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You already told us that, sir, and that wasn't my question. I moved on from that point. My question was: Did you have an office at the brigade command during that period of time, during the July 1995 period?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was your office in the brigade command? Where was it?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the brigade command, there was Pejic, the engineer's man, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you the location of your office, sir. I'm not -- and you seem to be answering something I didn't ask you. I'm not sure what you're referring to, but what was the location of your office?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand your question. I didn't have a separate office. We had a joint office or premises, the operations hall, where we would sit around frequently if we had to prepare any papers or anything like that. We'd do that in the premises of the Kaolin factory of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where were you during the days of 11, 12, and 13 July?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th, I was at the observation post, and that's when Srebrenica fell. On the 12th, I was at the firing lines collecting materiel and equipment, not me but the soldiers. I was present there. And on the 13th, I was also in my original unit where we were collecting up materiel and equipment, because we hadn't completed that part of the work in the Bratunac Brigade as regards defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And during that period of time, were you at any point at the brigade command? Did you go to the brigade command during that period?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure I did from time to time. But it wasn't binding; I didn't have the duty to do that. I had no need to do that. I just saw to it that the equipment was collected for the three firing positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on 12 and 13 July, did you see General Krstic or Mladic at the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to General Krstic, I met him one afternoon. I bumped into him briefly. Now, whether that was the 12th -- I think it was probably the 12th or perhaps on the 11th towards evening or the evening of the 12th. But I would say it was the 11th actually, towards evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see -- this was at the brigade command that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We bumped into each other in the hall or the operations hall. He asked me something, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you see General Mladic during that period at the command?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic, yes, I did see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many times you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't count the number of times, but I wasn't near him at all. I didn't have occasion to be near him, nor was that indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you saw him more than once at the brigade command during those days?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once, certainly; twice, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where did you spend your nights during those days, sir, 11, 12, and 13 July? Where did you spend your evening?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent every night, unless I was the duty officer -- if I was on duty, I slept -- if I wasn't on duty, I would sleep in my family home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where was your family home?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 200 metres to the west of the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall, sir, when it -- which day you saw General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was on the 11th, that famous day. I think I saw him before he left for the Fontana meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And there was a meeting at the Fontana Hotel that afternoon or evening?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was that particular evening; that's why I assume it was probably the 11th. Yes, I think it was in the evening on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Colonel Blagojevic during that period?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic, I can't remember the day I saw him. I did see him once. I know he was tired. He sort of looked all dark and unnatural-looking from the tiredness, from the general fatigue. But it was not a marathon meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "it was not a marathon meeting," I didn't quite catch that, sir. What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A meeting. That is to say it was a brief meeting. We just said: "Hello," nothing lengthy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You're referring to your meeting with Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just the meeting; whereas, the actual meeting with Colonel Blagojevic, I don't remember. The 14th in the evening, the 15th. The other was just a brief encounter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you see him when you had this brief encounter?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we bumped into each other in the hall of the brigade command, in the hallway. He was coming and I was going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And on what day was this?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember exactly. Probably there's somebody who'd be able to tell you better. Now, whether Colonel Blagojevic came on the 11th or the 12th, I don't know. I think he returned from the terrain on the evening of the 11th, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how did you know, sir, about the meeting that took place at the Fontana Hotel the night of the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to that meeting, I didn't know about it then. Today, everybody knows about it, so I do too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But earlier I thought you said you saw Mladic before he went to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's a mischaracterisation of the evidence. You can play back the testimony. That's not what he said. He speculated that he thinks that it was on the 11th because on that day he went to the meeting at Hotel Fontana. It's a total mischaracterisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's not a mischaracterisation. I believe that is what the witness said and I'm asking him to clarify. I don't think Mr. Karnavas needs to give his opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could find in the transcript what the witness said. We have a Defence counsel very picky.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to be able to find it in the transcript, Your Honours. So what I can perhaps do is rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you not tell us earlier that you saw General Mladic before he went to the Hotel Fontana on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I said, I shall repeat. I don't remember exactly whether I saw General Mladic on the 11th or on the 12th, but I seem to feel that I saw him in the afternoon of the 11th. Now, as to the meeting at the Fontana, which he held, I know about that now. But at that time, I was far too low down the chain of command and it wasn't up to me and my competence to know where -- General Mladic's whereabouts and who he was having a meeting with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm going to -- I've now found the portion of the transcript, sir, and I'm going to read it out to you what you just told us earlier. I believe that's at page 21, line -- starting at line 3. The question was: "Okay. Do you recall, sir, which day you saw General Mladic? Answer: "I think it was on the 11th, that famous day. I think I saw him before he left for the Fontana meeting." So you seem to know, sir, from that response that he was leaving for the Fontana meeting. So the question is: How did you know that he was leaving for the Fontana meeting?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying, after so much time has gone by, I know now many things, many more things than I knew then. Because none of us knew about that at that particular point in time. Perhaps I misunderstood your question. I know now about the meeting that took place; everybody knows about the meeting. But 1 million per cent at the time, I didn't know about the meeting. How would I know who the general was holding meetings with?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. All right. Moving on then to another area. You were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor investigators I believe in 2001, in November. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've told us yesterday that you've reviewed your transcript. Is that right? Before testifying, you've reviewed the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time, sir, when you were being asked questions by the investigator, you knew it was important to give as complete and as accurate information as possible. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this was a job I dealt with professionally, then it would have been 100 per cent correct. But speaking to someone three years later and then four years later, I can't put everything into chronological order. I abide 100 per cent by what I'm saying today, because now I know a lot more than I did then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you're telling us, sir, that in three years -- rather, in 2001, you don't abide 100 per cent by what you said to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. What I'm saying is: I can't put my replies in chronological order like that. Memories are not always the same. I do stand by the essence of what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But it would be fair to say, sir, that your memory would have been better about these events in 2001 than they are now. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you, because there are some things I didn't know then but I do now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you about the things that you've learned since that time, sir. I'm asking you about your memory of the events as you knew them at the time that the events occurred. Isn't it fair to say that your memory of these events at that time would have been better in 2001 than they are now?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to estimate that realistically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying your memory could have improved with time? Are you saying your memory is better now with these events than they were in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The details that stuck in my mind are something I will not forget for as long as I live, but I have probably forgotten some details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it would be fair to say, sir, that your memory of the events now would be -- would not be as clear as your memory of the events in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. This calls for speculation. This has been asked and answered as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would be fair to say, sir, that your memory of the events now would not be as clear as your memory of the events in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No. I think that my memory is about the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you did -- when you spoke to the investigators, sir, in 2001, did you try to be as complete and accurate as possible in your answers?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably yes, just as I am today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, yesterday, sir, you testified that Dragan Trisic was present when you received the order from Colonel Blagojevic to go to Zvornik. And you never mentioned that to the investigator when he initially interviewed you, did you?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, I couldn't recall this. Afterwards, I sat down with Dragan Trisic because we live in the same village or town, and we discussed the topic. And then I recalled this and he confirmed it. I recall that he was there, but he was there briefly and then he left. And I said that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I know you said it yesterday. My question was: You didn't say it -- you didn't tell the investigator at the time that you were interviewed in 2001. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably I felt it was not so important to mention Dragan Trisic. I thought it was more important to talk about my relationship with the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you also told us yesterday, sir, that you saw Major Eskic at Zvornik in the morning of 15 July. Do you remember telling us that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention that to the OTP investigator when he asked you in 2001, did you?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct, I didn't mention it, because I felt this detail was less important, whether Zoran Kovacevic or Major Eskic came. What was important to me was that the commander respected what we had agreed on, that I should return to my home unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm going to give you a copy of your transcript in the B/C/S version. And I'm going to ask you to turn to page 56.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in the English version, Your Honours, it's page 56, line 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The B/C/S version is page 56, paragraph 1 -- sorry, paragraph 3. The question at line 22, sir, is: "Did you see anyone from outside of the Zvornik Brigade, from Bratunac, from Sokolac, from the corps?" And you answered: "No. I was there at the time when Srebrenica was being finished and in the meantime probably the operation on Zepa was prepared and there was an exchange of units, defensive and operative units." So you were asked a specific question about this, whether you saw anyone from outside the Zvornik Brigade, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said then as I say now, that I didn't see anyone except the assistant duty officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were asked a general question, sir, whether you saw anyone from the Zvornik Brigade, from Bratunac, from Sokolac, from the corps, from outside the Zvornik Brigade. And you've told us yesterday that in the morning you saw Major Eskic and Kovacevic. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the question you put to me was whether I saw them when I arrived in Zvornik or when I left Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't the question that I put to you, sir. I think the question -- the question -- it was an answer that you answered yesterday from your in-chief testimony where you were asked who else was there in Zvornik. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zvornik when I was enumerating who was there, there was no one from the Bratunac Brigade in Zvornik. Rather, the officers who came to replace me were Major Dragan Eskic and Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So what you told us yesterday, sir, is that you saw those officers in Zvornik on the morning of the 15th yesterday. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the morning. I think I said between 11.00 and 12.00, because then I was able to see them because they had arrived from Bratunac to the command of the Zvornik Brigade to relieve me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you did not tell that to the investigator at the time that he interviewed you in 2001. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I felt there was no need, but I did tell the investigator that Commander Blagojevic fulfilled his promise and sent me relief. But who arrived --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that wasn't the question. You were asked if you had seen anybody else; that was the question. Now, I'm going to move on to another area.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break, I just have one more question. You also told us yesterday, sir, you mentioned that you requested on the 17th of July, you requested buses from Momir Nikolic, and you said that Momir told you that the prisoners were to be sent to Konjevic Polje. Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I asked the command of the Bratunac Brigade, when I asked for them, I spoke I think to Momir Nikolic, I asked him to send us buses because there were prisoners, and he said the prisoners should go to Konjevic Polje. And I assume it was logical for him to tell me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's what you testified to yesterday. Now, you never mentioned that to the investigator when he interviewed you in 2001, that you spoke to Momir Nikolic and that he told you to do this, did you?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. That was the first time I was being officially interviewed, as can be seen from the statement. And I didn't know what was supposed to be said, because it would have lasted for days and days and days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you said yesterday, sir, that Momir -- that the -- that you handed over the men to Dusko Jevic was Momir Nikolic told you to do that, to take -- and he was to take them to Konjevic Polje. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I handed those people over to Dusko Jevic, because Dusko Jevic was going with his unit in the direction of Konjevic Polje. And Momir, at the same time, was one of the main people as regards my brigade whom I could ask, because I think the commander then had gone off to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you were asked, sir, and this is at page 31 of the English transcript, and in yours page 30, paragraph 12. At line 9, sir, you were asked: "And the reason you handed them over to Jevic is because he is a police officer?" And you said: "No, no. After the operation was completed and the task was carried out, I had to return to my unit. I ordered them to call Bratunac and to send a bus to bring the soldiers back." And then you continue: "I think that" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down when reading. We don't have the text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. "I think, but I'm not sure that Jevic's unit was stationed in the area of Konjevic Polje during the operation." And then you go on. Nowhere there, sir, do you mention Momir Nikolic or getting in touch with him, do you?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably I omitted or forgot to say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see that, Your Honour, it is time for the break and I am about to move to another area. Perhaps it might be a good time to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I do have a few questions relating to when you arrived in Zvornik. Now, in your examination-in-chief you said when you were there that the deputy duty officer told you Obrenovic was sleeping. Do you remember you told us that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you didn't actually see Obrenovic, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't really know where he was, do you?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only from what the assistant duty officer told me, and he said that he was asleep, or rather, resting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So aside from being told that he was asleep, you personally have no idea where he was at the time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no idea, no. This was the only information I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you were at Zvornik, you said that you spent most of the time outside because it was summertime. You were outside for a period of time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was morning. I wasn't asleep. The soldiers were in one of the rooms. I was outside. There were benches, and we used to sit there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And while you were there, sir, did you see a bus full of Muslims there?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, maybe if we can go to exhibit number P134. If I can ask the assistance of Madam Usher. If we can put page 6 on the ELMO and provide a copy in the B/C/S version of that page to the witness. Okay. Now, you see towards the bottom of that report which is -- it's the barracks -- just for the record, it's the barracks report from Zvornik. And what we're looking at is the date of 14, 15 July, 1995. And it's entitled: "Report on situation in the barracks to the commander." Towards the bottom of that report, it states: "A bus with the prisoners stayed overnight at the compound of the barracks." And it continues: "A body of troops at the barracks was not counted due to the activities in the field and practically only operations duty officer, duty officer and guards were at the barracks."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If she can lay a foundation as to whether the gentleman was at the barracks or where the barracks are in relation to the headquarters. Because the gentleman, as I understand it, never indicated that he was at any barracks and maybe the barracks are adjacent to the compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, from the previous answer. The witness said: "I was outside. There were benches, and we used to sit there." So this is the foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, benches and barracks; barracks are usually where people sleep, Your Honour. I don't know whether the barracks are adjacent to this industrial compound called Standard. Because if she's trying to impeach the gentleman, at least he should be given an opportunity to know where these barracks are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think there is a big problem there. Let's see how the witness will answer that question, then we'll see whether we need further foundations for that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't see the bus with the prisoners there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd like you to turn then to the next page, which is dated 15, 16 July, page 7. If we can put that page on the ELMO, please. Now, just looking at the second --

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. You mean the 15th to the 16th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's the page we're looking at. Have you found it there? All right.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I can draw your attention, sir, to the second line or second paragraph at that page. It says: "About 1000 hours, or 1000 hours, a new shift of the Bratunac Brigade arrived which was sent to the field some time later." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this the group that came up with Zoran Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely that group, that's what I said in my testimony of yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like us, sir, to deal a little bit with what happened on the 15th of July, morning of the 15th of July. You told us that you met Milan Lukic there? Right? You can put that away now. We're not dealing with the documents. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say I saw Lukic. I didn't know his first name was Milan, but I saw him at the gate, at the entry to the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you did say that he was from Visegrad. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't know where he was from, but that I know now that he's from the area of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us a -- tell us again what happened about this meeting that you had with him.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was awaiting the other shift to arrive, I was at the gate. I met him there. There was a group of my soldiers behind me because we were waiting to go back. And he said: "You have to give me a certain number of men to go out on the ground with me." And I said: "No, this is my unit. You can't take my men. I can't give my men to anyone without orders from my commander." In this situation, Drago Nikolic was close by; I think he was a security officer, and the late Dule Nikolic, a schoolmate of mine. And they came across the say hello and told him to go away, that he had no business with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see Colonel Beara there at Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that man. I don't think I know the man at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you see a very tall, big man, older gentleman perhaps, with white hair, in addition to the people that you've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I came across or saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know, sir, that Milan Lukic belonged to the intervention unit as part of the Visegrad Brigade or unit?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was part of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I thought of him as -- how shall I put it? A freelancer, someone who goes out to loot. I didn't know he belonged to a brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska. This is the first time I'm hearing such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, didn't you tell us later you found out he was part of the Visegrad unit?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. What I said was that I heard he was from Visegrad, or rather, the area of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know Boban Indic?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never heard of that name or nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what did you think that Milan Lukic wanted your troops for?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly. I don't know what he wanted, but he couldn't come and take soldiers I was responsible for. I assume he was up to no good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, didn't you ask him?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You think he would have told me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask him?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't ask him. As I said, I told him he couldn't get any men from me, and that was the end of our conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you ask him?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, if I can say, it's better to keep out of the way than go somewhere you're not supposed to go, because people like him could do anything at any moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What made you think that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought he was not on my level of education or position, and I didn't feel I ought to talk to him at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you, sir, in the Bratunac Brigade command on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, I probably did occasionally go to the Bratunac Brigade. But then, I was on the firing lines of my units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know that Milan Lukic's intervention platoon was supposed to be at the Bratunac Brigade command on that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. If there is foundation for this, I would like the young lady to put it on the ELMO so we can all see it. What she thinks is irrelevant. So she can show us the document that says that Lukic was supposed to be there, that he had authorisation from Krstic, from Blagojevic, from Mladic, from Beara, from Kosoric, whoever she thinks. But this line of questioning is totally improper, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think so. This is a cross-examination. I believe that the party conducting cross-examination could ask any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, not if there is a lack of foundation. I would like to know where she is deriving this information that Lukic was supposed to be on the Bratunac Brigade on that point, on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did we hear some testimony in your case --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- that Lukic was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there were some intercepts in the Prosecution's case. I will be referring to them. I will be getting there. And I think Mr. Karnavas is a little impatient. And we are getting to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, as I indicated earlier, I would like the young lady to present the evidence to the gentleman, here is an intercept, here's what it says, what do you have to say. As opposed to asking him to speculate as to what somebody else is supposed to be doing based on an intercept. And I would like to know if there is some connection between that intercept and reality, what actually is happening on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, I do have a name. And I would ask Mr. Karnavas to treat me as respectfully as I treat him. Secondly, there is nothing improper with that question at all. We are getting to that. It's a step-by-step process, as Mr. Karnavas, I'm sure, knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the Prosecution is asking a question to see whether this person is there and whether the witness saw this person or not. And we'll see whether we need any further foundations when the question is going on. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you know that Milan Lukic's intervention platoon was supposed to be at the Bratunac Brigade command on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the bus broke down -- their bus broke down that day?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm going to refer then to Exhibit P216 and ask that the English version be placed on the ELMO. Now, you see that there, sir? There's a conversation going on at 1919 on that day, and it says: "Do you have any bus there? "I have this one which is a reserve. "Send it. Send that bus towards Visegrad, Podromanija, Rogatica, and further. When he comes across a bus with a group of soldiers, those are the ones from Visegrad. Boban is their commander." "Say again? "Boban Indic. And then bring them to the command in Bratunac." So you weren't aware of that. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never heard of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This was posed in a manner that somehow Lukic was being tied into it. I suspect there's another intercept. I don't know. I don't see any Lukic here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We are getting to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Also I object on the grounds of relevancy. What does this gentleman have to do with this particular intercept? Also I don't see who is identified as X and Y. Who are these people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe the matter will be more clear when is proceeding is going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go to exhibit P245. If we can put that on the ELMO, please. Now, sir, there's a conversation on 15 July, 0957 between Colonel Beara and Krstic. This is Beara speaking. If you look at the very middle of the conversation, about 18 lines down. It says: "Look. I need 15 to 30 men with Boban Indic. I can't do anything. Yes." And then the next line says: "Indic, Indic, Lukic's deputy, 15 to 30 men. I can't do anything." Do you see that's there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you know that Radomir Furtula was Lukic's commander.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go to the next intercept. Did you know that Furtula was the commander at the Visegrad Brigade of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Going then to P244. And if we can have the English version placed on the ELMO. Thank you, Madam Usher. At 954 hours, 15 July. It's a conversation between General Zivanovic and Colonel Beara. You see about halfway through the page, Beara says: "You know that day, I informed the commander about it, Furtula didn't send Lukic's intervention platoon." Zivanovic says: "And Lukic is waiting at Blagojevic." Beara: "Lukic is here with me and his driver and we urged that." Zivanovic: "Yes." Beara: "Yesterday, Furtula sent one soldier without an arm and another one that Lukic knows is a drunk," and it goes on. Do you know why, sir, General Zivanovic thinks Lukic was at the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object on the grounds that it calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, he can tell us, Your Honour, whether he knows or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there may be some speculations, but it doesn't matter if you put this question to this witness. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything from this area on that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If a unit, sir, comes from Bratunac -- from another command, would it be normal for them to report to the Bratunac Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would report to the duty officer according to some sort of order, if it came on the basis of command responsibility. Now, because, as I've been telling you that I was on that day a long way from the command, maybe I came in from time to time. Who was there I wouldn't really notice. I would come in on my own business; if I had to come it was for a purpose. And then I would just come and go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you see in this intercept, in this conversation, sir, it also says that -- Beara says that: "Lukic is here with me and his driver." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Had I seen Lukic, I would have been Beara. But as I didn't see Lukic - and I said I saw him in the morning in Zvornik - I didn't see him after that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this conversation was -- as the evidence shows, sir, that Beara was in Zvornik on that day. And you say you didn't see Beara?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Zvornik is a big place. The command is a big place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We understand that. We'll hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not see either in Zvornik or Bratunac, Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, it's the Prosecution contention, sir, that Mr. Beara was with Dragan Nikolic and Milan Lukic at Zvornik and you didn't see them there?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Dragan Nikolic, I don't think so. Perhaps with Drago Nikolic, but that's not within my area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps we can then move on to the 17 July. On your examination-in-chief yesterday, sir, you told us that you were in charge of the soldiers and that Dusko Jevic was in charge of the police and that you were, in fact, equal partners. Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Dusko Jevic has said that he was actually resubordinated to the Bratunac Brigade because he was receiving orders from them. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that during that period of time Colonel Blagojevic was in command of the MUP units and other units along the road?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I knew was that Colonel Blagojevic was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, but not about the individual units. And I don't know that that was how it was to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's go to Exhibit 495. Now, if you look at page 1 of that exhibit under the heading: "Proposal." And I believe it's towards the end of that first page. It says: "To authorise and appoint the commander of the Bratunac Brigade as commander of all forces, which participating in searching the terrain and sweeping the battlefield to the east of the road (and in control of the Kasaba/Drinjaca road), because we have no one to appoint from the command of the Drina Corps." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about this order. This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is an order from Colonel Milanovic regarding the engagement of forces and searching the terrain in the direction of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. It's not an order; it's a proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we haven't seen the first part of this document. We just see this paragraph it's entitled with: "Proposal."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's a proposal, not an order. This gentleman cannot order. He makes a proposal to General Krstic. General Krstic then can order, but he's not in a position to give orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take it as a proposal. You may proceed

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's dated 15 July, for the record. Do you see that there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's go to Exhibit P496. Now, if we go to paragraph 2 -- first of all, this is from the command of the Bratunac Brigade, and it's dated 16 July 1995. It's a daily combat report. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name of the commander, Blagojevic, is on the bottom. Right?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we go to paragraph 2, at about the fifth line in that paragraph, it says: "We made preparations to dispatch two companies of the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade (100 soldiers) and the reconnaissance platoon of the Infantry Battalion. During the day, the brigade commander visited all units which are blocking the enemy retreat (the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, units of the 65th Protection Motorised Regiment, parts of the MUP, and the 5th Engineering Battalion), defined their tasks and organised their joint action and communications. Because of the engagement of forces of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade and the Milici Brigade on other tasks and assignments, execution of the task of searching the terrain has been slowed down and actions to block enemy forces in the aforementioned area have been hampered." Were you aware that Colonel Blagojevic visited these units?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And doesn't that say, sir, that Colonel Blagojevic was commander of these forces that were searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read this combat report, and I'm not informed about it. I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us, sir, what happened to the captured men on 17 July, the Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on that 17th, when I was with the units of the Bratunac Brigade and with Dusko Jevic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MICO GAVRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, and I said yesterday that those units, or rather, those men were taken to Konjevic Polje, to the crossroads there, the Zvornik/Sarajevo crossroads, where there was an old warehouse. And in a day or two, I was going privately to Sokolac, and I happened to pass by and see those people there. And they were being secured by a special police unit. I wanted to see those people, whether they were the people. So I crossed. A policeman tried to stop me, but somebody shouted out to him to let me pass by. I saw the people, they were there. And some of those people were collecting up some papers around the building, and the others were sitting inside. That's as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say you saw them at this warehouse, is that where there is a gas station there today?
